activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence supports the claim about cycle lanes?
activities.passage: More cycle lanes would make short journeys safer. ___ This would encourage people to leave their cars at home.

options.text: They would separate cyclists from heavy traffic.
The library has a new fiction section.
The park closes at sunset.
The timetable was printed yesterday.

activities.explanation: The sentence gives a reason for the safety claim.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence follows the evidence about bus delays?
activities.passage: Several passengers reported late buses. ___ As a result, some people arrived after their shifts had begun.

options.text: The delays were especially common on the evening route.
The museum displays modern paintings.
The café sells soup at lunchtime.
The room has three windows.

activities.explanation: The missing sentence narrows the evidence before its consequence.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence gives an example of safer crossings?
activities.passage: The road near the school needs better protection for pedestrians. ___ This measure would be particularly useful at the morning arrival time.

options.text: For instance, a raised crossing could slow approaching cars.
The school choir rehearses on Thursdays.
The sports hall needs new curtains.
The village has a small post office.

activities.explanation: For instance introduces a relevant concrete measure.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence gives the result of cleaner-air measures?
activities.passage: Fewer cars would improve air quality near the school. ___ Parents could also feel more confident about walking there.

options.text: This change would reduce the amount of traffic at the gate.
The school kitchen serves breakfast at eight.
The local shop closes on Mondays.
The bus has blue seats.

activities.explanation: The sentence explains how the proposed change would work.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the paragraph.
activities.prompt: Which topic sentence introduces the library argument?
activities.passage: ___ Many residents work during the day and cannot visit before six.

options.text: Libraries should offer at least one later opening each week.
The library bought new chairs.
A book was returned on Tuesday.
The café is next to the library.

activities.explanation: The first sentence states the paragraph's central claim.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which concession fits the insulation argument?
activities.passage: Home insulation can lower energy use. ___ Even so, the long-term savings make it worth considering.

options.text: Although the initial cost is high, the improvement has lasting benefits.
The roof was painted last summer.
The family bought a new sofa.
The energy bill arrived yesterday.

activities.explanation: Although introduces the cost concession before the positive return.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence provides a contrast about online appointments?
activities.passage: Online appointments are quick for many users. ___ A phone option should therefore remain available.

options.text: However, some residents do not have reliable internet access.
The office painted its waiting room.
The receptionist takes lunch at noon.
The website uses a blue logo.

activities.explanation: However introduces the limitation that justifies the second sentence.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly refers to the survey evidence?
activities.passage: The survey found that waiting times were the main complaint. ___ The office should review its appointment system.

options.text: This evidence suggests that delays are affecting user satisfaction.
The office has a green front door.
The survey was printed in colour.
Some appointments take place upstairs.

activities.explanation: This evidence clearly refers to the stated survey finding.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence introduces a consequence of fewer calls?
activities.passage: The new online form gives users the information they need. ___ Staff can spend more time on complex enquiries.

options.text: As a result, routine phone calls have become less frequent.
The office opens at nine.
The form is available in two colours.
Users sometimes bring paper copies.

activities.explanation: As a result connects the information to the benefit for staff.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the paragraph.
activities.prompt: Which sentence closes the public-park argument?
activities.passage: Public parks give residents space to exercise and meet. They also support local wildlife. ___

options.text: For these reasons, their maintenance should remain a council priority.
The council office has a new lift.
A football match was cancelled.
The park gate is made of metal.

activities.explanation: For these reasons links the conclusion to both benefits.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence supports the library-access claim?
activities.passage: Libraries should open later once a week. ___ This would allow more workers to borrow books after work.

options.text: Many residents finish work after the current closing time.
The library has a wooden desk.
The librarian enjoys historical novels.
The building was opened in 1982.

activities.explanation: The sentence explains why later opening would help.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which example belongs after the food-waste claim?
activities.passage: Schools can reduce food waste without changing the whole menu. ___ This would prevent unopened food from being thrown away.

options.text: For example, they could offer surplus portions at the end of lunch.
The kitchen has four large windows.
The pupils study geography on Fridays.
The menu is printed each morning.

activities.explanation: The example is a practical way to reduce the stated waste.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence gives a precise reference to the pilot?
activities.passage: The pilot reduced average waiting time by ten minutes. ___ It therefore appears to have improved access for participants.

options.text: This reduction in waiting time was recorded during the four-week trial.
The office has white walls.
The pilot team travelled by train.
Some users prefer morning appointments.

activities.explanation: The reference names the reduction and limits its time frame.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence moves from evidence to action?
activities.passage: Residents repeatedly mentioned the unsafe crossing. ___ The council should install a raised crossing.

options.text: This evidence indicates that the current arrangement needs to change.
The road is closed on Sundays.
Residents meet in the nearby hall.
The council uses electric cars.

activities.explanation: The sentence interprets the repeated evidence before the proposal.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence balances the free-transport proposal?
activities.passage: Free transport would help students reach college. ___ A small pilot could show whether the benefits justify the cost.

options.text: Although the scheme would be expensive, it could improve attendance.
The college has a new noticeboard.
Some students bring packed lunches.
The buses are painted red.

activities.explanation: Although links the benefit with the relevant cost concern.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence introduces the paper-form concession?
activities.passage: Digital forms can speed up applications. ___ An alternative should still be available.

options.text: Nevertheless, they may exclude people without reliable internet access.
The application has four pages.
The office bought new computers.
Applicants often use blue pens.

activities.explanation: Nevertheless marks the contrast that supports an alternative.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence avoids a vague reference to the scheme?
activities.passage: The new booking scheme has reduced missed appointments. ___ This improvement should be monitored over the next quarter.

options.text: The reduction in missed appointments suggests that reminders are working.
The reception desk is near the window.
The scheme was announced in June.
Appointments are usually twenty minutes long.

activities.explanation: The noun phrase identifies the precise improvement.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence links better signs to fewer enquiries?
activities.passage: Visitors often ask where the meeting rooms are. ___ Staff would then have more time for other tasks.

options.text: Clearer signs could therefore reduce routine enquiries.
The meeting rooms have wooden tables.
Visitors usually arrive by bus.
The staff kitchen is upstairs.

activities.explanation: Therefore links the observed issue to a plausible response.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence adds a distinct concern without repetition?
activities.passage: The online system is efficient for regular users. ___ The service should therefore keep a phone option.

options.text: A further concern is that new users may find the instructions unclear.
The system was launched in April.
Regular users receive emails.
The office has a telephone.

activities.explanation: A further concern advances the paragraph with a new issue.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence returns to the main claim after a concession?
activities.passage: Some residents are concerned about the cost of the proposal. ___ It would nevertheless improve access for people without cars.

options.text: Even so, the long-term social benefit should be considered.
The proposal is printed on recycled paper.
Residents met on Wednesday.
The car park is often full.

activities.explanation: Even so acknowledges the concern and restores the argument.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence limits a claim about a small pilot?
activities.passage: The pilot was successful for the participants who attended. ___ It should not yet be presented as proof that the scheme works everywhere.

options.text: This result applies to the pilot group and its four-week period.
The pilot used a white sign.
Participants received a welcome email.
The scheme has a short name.

activities.explanation: The sentence narrows both group and time.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence connects a concession to solar-panel savings?
activities.passage: Solar panels require an initial investment. ___ The long-term reduction in energy costs makes the plan worth examining.

options.text: Although the cost is significant, the panels could lower household bills.
The roof is made of tiles.
The family moved in May.
The energy company sends paper bills.

activities.explanation: The missing sentence contains both the concession and the benefit.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence connects repeated interviews with a proposal?
activities.passage: The same problem appeared in several interviews. ___ The service should test a clearer process before expanding it.

options.text: This repeated evidence suggests that the current process needs attention.
The interviews lasted ten minutes.
The service uses a digital calendar.
Some interviewees travelled by train.

activities.explanation: The sentence interprets repeated evidence before the recommendation.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence precisely describes the effect of the alternative route?
activities.passage: The alternative route avoids the closed bridge. ___ This could make journeys shorter for residents in the north.

options.text: It also connects directly with the northern bus stop.
The bridge was built of stone.
The route is marked in yellow.
Residents usually travel at noon.

activities.explanation: The sentence gives the missing link between route and shorter journey.

activities.instructions: Choose the sentence that completes the argument.
activities.prompt: Which sentence gives the final recommendation for an access trial?
activities.passage: The evidence shows that evening access is limited, while daytime sessions are well used. ___ This would test demand without changing the whole service.

options.text: For these reasons, the council should fund a one-year evening trial.
The council building has two entrances.
Daytime sessions begin at eight.
The service uses a monthly calendar.

activities.explanation: The recommendation follows both findings and the final sentence explains its scale.
